title: Common Vietnamese Dishes in Pregnancy: What to Keep, Tweak, or Skip
excerpt: Nutritionist-style analysis of phở, bún, cơm tấm, trứng ốp la and street snacks — safer prep, smart pairings, and what to leave out
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, a healthy diet is crucial for the development of the fetus and the health of the mother. However, with the diversity of Vietnamese cuisine, many pregnant women are often unsure about what dishes to keep, tweak, or skip. In this article, we will analyze common Vietnamese dishes and provide nutrition advice to help pregnant women have a safe and healthy diet.

## Analysis of Common Vietnamese Dishes
### Phở
Phở is one of the most popular Vietnamese dishes. To ensure food safety, pregnant women should choose phở made with cooked beef or chicken and avoid phở with raw or undercooked meat. Additionally, pregnant women should limit their consumption of phở, as it can be high in salt and fat.

### Bún
Bún is another popular Vietnamese dish, often served with a broth or grilled meat. Pregnant women should choose bún made with cooked meat and avoid bún with raw or undercooked meat. Additionally, pregnant women should limit their consumption of bún, as it can be high in carbohydrates and fat.

### Cơm tấm
Cơm tấm is a popular dish in Southern Vietnam. Pregnant women should choose cơm tấm made with cooked rice and avoid cơm tấm with raw or undercooked meat. Additionally, pregnant women should limit their consumption of cơm tấm, as it can be high in carbohydrates and fat.

### Trứng ốp la
Trứng ốp la is a simple but nutritious dish. Pregnant women should choose eggs that are cooked thoroughly and avoid raw or undercooked eggs, as they can contain salmonella. Additionally, pregnant women should limit their consumption of eggs, as they can be high in cholesterol.

### Street Snacks
Street snacks are a common part of Vietnamese cuisine. However, pregnant women should choose snacks that are cooked thoroughly and avoid snacks that are raw or undercooked, as they can contain bacteria or viruses. Additionally, pregnant women should limit their consumption of snacks, as they can be high in salt, sugar, and fat.

## Nutrition Advice
To have a safe and healthy diet, pregnant women should follow these guidelines:
* Choose foods that are cooked thoroughly
* Avoid foods that are raw or undercooked
* Limit consumption of foods that are high in salt, sugar, and fat
* Choose foods that are rich in nutrients
* Drink plenty of water and limit consumption of sugary drinks or caffeine

## Conclusion
A healthy diet is crucial for the development of the fetus and the health of the mother. With the diversity of Vietnamese cuisine, pregnant women should choose foods that are cooked thoroughly, avoid foods that are raw or undercooked, and limit their consumption of foods that are high in salt, sugar, and fat. For more information on pregnancy nutrition, you can visit our [meal planner](/planner) or [read more about related topics](/blog/topics).

## When to Seek Help
If you have any questions or concerns about your diet, you should seek help from a healthcare provider or a registered dietitian. They can provide you with personalized advice and guidance to help you have a safe and healthy diet.

* [Q: What should I eat during pregnancy?](#)
Pregnant women should eat foods that are cooked thoroughly, avoid foods that are raw or undercooked, and limit their consumption of foods that are high in salt, sugar, and fat.
* [Q: Can I eat phở during pregnancy?](#)
Pregnant women can eat phở, but should choose phở made with cooked beef or chicken and avoid phở with raw or undercooked meat.
* [Q: What should I drink during pregnancy?](#)
